subject: Clarify micro-floor allocation and context amortization for long-stream billing
messages:
From: Liz Harmon <liz.harmon@finboxhealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: sales_ops@finboxhealth.com, alan.choi@finboxhealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Question on micro-floor apportionment + long streaming contexts

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Two follow-ups from our architecture and finance teams about pricing mechanics before we proceed:

1) We run long streaming sessions for clinical note summarization (avg 6k tokens per session, occasional 20k spikes). How do you apply the micro-floor/minimums across streaming tokens vs. per-call billable units? Is there any amortization for long sessions so we don't get floored on every short heartbeat?

2) If we commit to a monthly baseline, can we have the micro-floor applied as a pooled credit across requests (apportioned), or is it enforced per-request and causes leakage when we have many concurrent short heartbeats?

3) Our engineers also asked about rounding: do you round token counts at the subtoken level, and what granularity do you bill (1 token, 10 token quantum, etc.)? We care because small rounding steps at high QPS skew our forecasts.

Attaching our sample QPS traces and an example request trace. Appreciate a short worked example and recommended config for us to avoid surprise overages.

-Liz
Liz Harmon
Head of Platform
FinBox Health

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Liz Harmon <liz.harmon@finboxhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question on micro-floor apportionment + long streaming contexts

Hi Liz — great questions, and good materials. I pulled together a short explainer and a worked example (attached). TL;DR answers up front:

- Micro-floor application: by default our hosted billing applies a small per-request minimum for token metering to prevent abusive nanobilling; for streaming calls we treat each continuous session as a single metered request (so long as the session remains active and uses the same stream id), which avoids repeated micro-floor charges on heartbeat tokens.

- Commit pooling: if you sign a monthly committed baseline we can convert the micro-floor into a pooled credit that gets consumed against total token usage (apportioned). That is a standard concession for customers with predictable traffic: it prevents leakage from many short calls.

- Rounding/quantum: tokenization happens with our tokenizer (BPE). We bill at the token level; the official unit is 1 token. For performance reasons we bucket meter events into a 10-token quantum for real-time invoicing (internal aggregation) but invoices show precise token counts and credits. When you have high QPS the effective rounding error is washed out; for low-volume heartbeat traffic we apply the pooled credit option to neutralize the quantum.

Worked example (see attached "pricing_example_v2.xlsx"):
- Scenario: 1k short sessions/day (heartbeat-only requests sending 12 tokens each) + 50 long sessions/day (avg 6k tokens)
- If micro-floor is enforced per-request (no pooling) and quantum=10 tokens, the 1k short sessions would each incur a 10-token floor -> 10k tokens of effective billing (vs. 12k actual) — not terrible, but with 1 token quanta they'd be floored to 12 per request depending on alignment.
- With pooling under a $10k/month commit we apportion those floors into the commit pool. Net effect: short-session leakage becomes a line-item in the committed usage bucket and does not create per-request floors on your invoice.

Recommendation: adopt a 3-month commit that converts micro-floor leakage into a pooled credit and enable "session-affinity" for streaming connections so each session is billed as a single metered request. For immediate relief we can issue a one-time smoothing credit for the pilot month.

I'm looping Marissa and Karthik on the commercial and contract details for the commit + pooled-credit language.

Attachments: pricing_example_v2.xlsx, context-billing-math.pdf

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Question on micro-floor apportionment + long streaming contexts

Camila / Karthik — forwarding FinBox's Qs. Key commercial points to confirm before we propose language to legal:

1) Commit sizing: what minimum commit ($/month) do we require to enable pooled micro-floor credits? Camila suggested $10k — confirm if that's our current threshold or negotiable for strategic pilots.

2) Reporting: Finance wants explicit invoice line-items that show "Micro-floor smoothing credit" so the customer sees the pooling effect. Do we have an existing invoice template that exposes that?

3) SLA/usage reconciliation window: they want monthly reconciliation and the ability to carry over unused pooled micro-floor credits for one billing cycle only. Is that acceptable?

Karthik, can you confirm the technical enforcement: session-affinity detection for streams and the edge case when a stream is disconnected and reconnected (do we start a new metered request or continue the session)? We need exact wording for the MSA.

-M

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Question on micro-floor apportionment + long streaming contexts

Marissa / Camila — technical confirmation and suggested MSA wording below. Short answers first:

- Session affinity: we bind stream sessions to a single metered request when the client uses a stable session id and TLS connection stays open. If the client reconnects with the same session id within a 60s grace window, we continue the same meter; beyond that we treat it as a new request.

- Commit threshold: commercial can gate pooled micro-floor conversion at $8k/month for strategic pilots, $10k/month as standard. We can flex for enterprise deals.

- Rounding: meter records are generated at token granularity; invoice reconciliation uses the precise token count. The 10-token aggregation quantum is purely for internal aggregation latency; it does not create permanent rounding on the invoice.

Suggested MSA clause (plain language for legal to massage):
"For customers with a qualifying monthly commitment (minimum $8,000), Redwood will apply micro-floor smoothing: per-request minimum billable units (micro-floors) will be aggregated into a pooled credit and deducted from the customer's committed usage each billing cycle. Unused pooled micro-floor credits may be carried forward for a single subsequent billing cycle. Session affinity for streaming requests is defined as continuity of session id within a 60 second reconnect window; disconnected sessions re-established after the reconnect window are treated as new billable requests."

I'll also upload a short internal note to BILL-612 with the edge-case tests (disconnect scenarios + token alignment fuzz). Camila, if you want I can draft a short appendix for the SOW that lists exact numeric examples for their traffic profile.

-Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Billing
